headline: RBI SAC reviews MSME credit flow; DG urges faster sanctions, less collateral
summary_points: 31st RBI Standing Advisory Committee meeting on MSME credit flow held in Kolkata on 27 November 2026, chaired by Deputy Governor Swaminathan J.
Banks urged to expedite credit sanctions and reduce collateral reliance via cash-flow-based lending using ULI and other digital channels.
Greater use of TReDS for receivables financing and early identification and resolution of stress was advocated.
Committee reviewed working capital and investment credit, first-time borrowers and credit guarantee coverage.
Discussed higher collateral-free lending limit for micro and small enterprises, CPSE invoice settlement via TReDS and key MSMED (Amendment) Act, 2026 provisions.
who_is_affected: Banks, NBFCs, MSMEs, MSME associations and finance teams dealing with MSME credit, TReDS and receivables financing.
action_required: Banks and MSMEs should note the stated focus on cash-flow-based lending and TReDS, and review MSME lending and receivables financing practices accordingly.

social.linkedin:
RBI has held the 31st meeting of its Standing Advisory Committee on MSME credit flow in Kolkata, chaired by Deputy Deputy Governor Shri Swaminathan J.

Key messages for banks:
- Expedite credit sanctions
- Reduce reliance on collateral through cash-flow-based lending using ULI and other digital channels
- Make greater use of TReDS for receivables financing
- Identify and resolve stress early

The Committee reviewed working capital and investment credit, lending to first-time borrowers and credit guarantee coverage. It also discussed the higher collateral-free lending limit for micro and small enterprises, settlement of CPSE invoices through TReDS and key provisions of the MSMED (Amendment) Act, 2026.

Industry associations were invited to take part in RBI town halls and district-level MSME SAMVAAD meetings.

This is a press release and not a new directive, but it signals supervisory priorities for MSME lending.

Please verify details with the official RBI press release (2026-2027/1581).

🏦 RBI's MSME credit review is out!

At the 31st SAC meeting in Kolkata, the Deputy Governor urged banks to:
✅ Sanction credit faster
✅ Rely less on collateral
✅ Use cash-flow-based lending via ULI
✅ Use TReDS for receivables financing

The MSMED (Amendment) Act, 2026 and the higher collateral-free limit were also discussed. 📊
